html:
In 1397 the Byzantine scholar Manuel Chrysoloras began teaching Greek in Florence, the start of a stream of Greek teachers, books and ideas into Italy.

For centuries few people in western Europe could read Greek. Florentine humanists wanted the ancient authors in the original, and they invited Chrysoloras to teach. His students, among them Leonardo Bruni, translated Plato and others into Latin, and his grammar was used for generations.

More Greeks followed as the Ottomans closed in on Byzantium. Gemistos Plethon lectured at the Council of Florence, and Bessarion settled in Italy and collected hundreds of Greek manuscripts. After the fall of Constantinople in 1453 more scholars came. In the 1490s the Venetian printer Aldus Manutius began printing the Greek classics. Together they gave the Renaissance direct access to Greek philosophy, science and literature.
sum: In 1397 the Byzantine scholar Manuel Chrysoloras began teaching Greek in Florence, the start of a stream of Greek teachers, books and ideas into Italy.
